fields.why: Median sex partners (3 vs 1.5) is compared between vaccination groups and interpreted as a risk factor, and the 8.4-month vaccination-to-diagnosis median is set against the French cluster, so 'compared or interpreted' favours continuous (B). A is defensible because partner counts are a characteristic of cases, which the brief says does not make an outcome continuous.

brief_issues: The two continuous-outcome rules collide when a case characteristic (e.g. number of partners) is compared between groups; say which wins.
